## Additional Features - **Building Collision** — A buildings index is included for all non-filtered buildings, each carrying a per-building foundation depth in in-game meters. Depths scale with building height and footprint width and are bounded to the **−10 m** to **−80 m** range: single-family homes and low-rise structures anchor at the floor, while the tallest towers reach toward the cap. Freestanding towers, masts, chimneys, and other slender non-occupiable structures are detected by shape and floored to the **−10 m** minimum. Foundation depths drive underground tunnel-clearance collision and are also emitted as a visual `foundations` pmtiles layer visible on the in-game map. Building footprints come from the Overture Maps Foundation with heights enriched from the Global Building Atlas (GBA LoD1) and the JRC GHS-OBAT registry as fallback tiers. - **Water Depth Index** — A water depth index restricts track placement in water bodies. Hungary is landlocked, so all water (the Danube and Tisza rivers, Lake Balaton, Lake Velence, canals and oxbows) uses a flat **−5 m** inland index that prevents surface-level track placement while keeping tunnels viable. - **Place Name Labels** — Three layers of place name labels are embedded in the map: - _City labels_ — Budapest and the megyei jogú város (cities with county rights) at the metropolitan scale. - _Municipality labels_ — Names of all települések (settlements) within the map boundary, plus the 23 named kerületek (districts) of Budapest. - _Neighborhood labels_ — Sub-settlement blocks derived from the cadastral street network, indexed within each település (including külterület — outer, non-built-up areas). ## Methodology This map is generated through a six-phase pipeline that transforms Hungarian government census, cadastral, and employment statistics into georeferenced origin/destination demand points. **Point Seeding:** Candidate points are placed within each sub-settlement block using population-weighted centroids derived from KSH's Népszámlálás 2022 census-block layer (over one million blocks nationally) blended with the KSH INSPIRE 1 km population grid, dasymetrically refined against building footprints. Sub-settlement blocks themselves are cut from the national cadastre (TAKAROS), whose public-road parcels form the block boundaries — the same block fabric a Hungarian city map draws. A building-level dual-allocation pass then promotes points to mixed residential/workplace state wherever a point is the nearest carrier for buildings of both kinds. **Mesh Reconciliation:** Initial point populations are refined by solving a constrained convex optimization that approximates each point's mass to residential and economic mesh ideals while preserving Népszámlálás 2022 totals for each település (and each Budapest kerület). **Aggregation:** A global scaling factor reconciles boundary-captured employed residents against workplace jobs. Workplace mass is derived from a multi-tier building-use cascade — Copernicus Urban Atlas 2021 land use, JRC GHS-OBAT building attributes, OSM and Overture Places points-of-interest, and an ML land-cover fallback — calibrated per settlement against KSH's census workplace ground truth via non-negative least squares. **Commute Assignment:** Commute flows are assigned using a gravity model with distance-decay, calibrated against KSH's Népszámlálás 2022 commuting matrices: the megye-level residence × workplace table plus per-település own-settlement containment shares, reconciled via Generalized IPF. Commuters whose census workplace lies beyond the map boundary are routed to boundary gateway points along their real outbound corridors, preserving macro flow directions at the map edge. **Special Demand Injection:** Non-commuter demand generators — the airport, hospitals and polyclinics, universities, museums, theatres and cultural centres, libraries, thermal baths (gyógyfürdők), stadiums, racetracks, and other attractions — are injected as an additive layer. **Layout Reconciliation:** A final spatial pass resolves point overlaps and ensures map clickability while keeping special-demand locations fixed. ## Data Sources All demand modeling is derived from freely available Hungarian government statistical datasets and public geospatial resources. ### Census & Demographics -
